# pocketid_client_secret (Resource)

Manages a secret of an OIDC client in Pocket-ID. A client can have several secrets at the same time (up to 20, expired ones included), and each of them authenticates the client. Pocket ID has no way to change a secret, so changing any argument replaces it.

Pocket ID stores only a hash of the secret. Either supply the value in the write-only `secret_wo` argument, so that it is never stored in the plan or the state, or let Pocket ID generate it and read it from `value`, which is stored in the state.

~> **Note** A public client has no secrets, so Pocket ID rejects a secret for a client with `is_public = true`.

## Example Usage

### Write-only secret

`secret_wo` is a [write-only argument](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments): Terraform sends it to Pocket ID and stores it in neither the plan nor the state. Pass it from an [ephemeral](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/values/variables#exclude-values-from-state) variable or resource, so that it is not stored anywhere in Terraform. Terraform cannot see a change of a write-only argument, so increment `secret_wo_version` to replace the secret with a new value.

```terraform
variable "api_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "pocketid_client" "api" {
  name          = "API Service Client"
  callback_urls = ["https://api.example.com/oauth/callback"]
}

resource "pocketid_client_secret" "api" {
  client_id = pocketid_client.api.id

  secret_wo         = var.api_client_secret
  secret_wo_version = 1
}
```

### Generated secret

Without `secret_wo`, Pocket ID generates the secret and returns it once, when it creates it. The value is in `value`, which is sensitive and stored in the state.

```terraform
resource "pocketid_client_secret" "generated" {
  client_id = pocketid_client.api.id

  # Optional: the secret stops working at this time.
  expires_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

output "api_client_secret" {
  value     = pocketid_client_secret.generated.value
  sensitive = true
}
```

### Rotating a secret

A client can have several secrets at once, so a new secret can be created before the old one is deleted. Give each secret its own resource and remove the old one once its users have moved on.

## Notes

- Pocket ID stores a hash of each secret, so the value of a secret cannot be read back. `value` is set only when Pocket ID generated the secret and is null otherwise, including after an import.
- A client can have at most 20 secrets, expired ones included.
- A public client (`is_public = true`) has no secrets, and Pocket ID rejects a secret for it.
- A secret that is deleted in Pocket ID is removed from the state and created again on the next apply.
- Pocket ID cannot change a secret, so changing `client_id`, `expires_at` or `secret_wo_version` replaces it. `expires_at` is compared as written, so a different notation of the same time also replaces the secret.
- When Pocket ID's `autoCreateOidcClientSecret` setting is on, which is its default, a new confidential client gets a secret that no resource tracks. Set `AUTO_CREATE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=false` on the Pocket ID server (Pocket ID reads it only when `UI_CONFIG_DISABLED=true`; otherwise turn the setting off in the application settings) so that the secrets of a client are exactly your `pocketid_client_secret` resources. See the [`pocketid_client`](client.md) resource.

## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) The ID of the OIDC client the secret belongs to. Changing it replaces the secret.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `expires_at` (String) When the secret stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in the future. The secret does not expire when this is not set. Use whole seconds: Pocket ID's default SQLite storage keeps no finer time. Changing it replaces the secret.
- `secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The value of the secret, as a write-only argument that is never stored in the plan or the state. It must have at least 16 characters, all of them printable ASCII. When it is not set, Pocket ID generates the secret and returns it in `value`. Changing it does not change the secret on its own; increment `secret_wo_version` to replace the secret with the new value.
- `secret_wo_version` (Number) Version of `secret_wo`. Changing it replaces the secret, which is how a new `secret_wo` takes effect, because Terraform cannot see a change of a write-only argument. Requires `secret_wo`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the secret was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `id` (String) The ID of the client secret, as assigned by Pocket ID.
- `prefix` (String) The first characters of the secret, which Pocket ID keeps in clear text so that its secrets can be told apart. Empty for secrets Pocket ID migrated from before it supported several secrets per client.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The value of the secret, set only when Pocket ID generated it because `secret_wo` was not given, and null otherwise. Pocket ID returns it once, when it creates the secret.

## Import

A client secret is imported with the ID of its client and its own ID, separated by a `/`. The ID of a secret is shown in the Pocket ID API (`GET /api/oidc/clients/{id}/secrets`).

```shell
terraform import pocketid_client_secret.example <client_id>/<secret_id>
```

The value of an imported secret is not known, so `value` is null. To manage the secret's value from then on, replace it by setting `secret_wo` and `secret_wo_version`.
